newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY LEAGUE-ARTHURSON RESIGNS BECAUSE OF HEALTH.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE-ARTHURSON RESIGNS BECAUSE OF HEALTH.

text.p: The Australian Rugby League (ARL) lost its second senior executive in two months on Wednesday when chairman Ken Arthurson announced he had resigned for health reasons.
The resignation of Arthurson, who led the sport's established ruling body in Australia for 14 years, follows that of general manager John Quayle two months ago.
Quayle left the ARL to take up a senior post with the organising committee for the Sydney 2000 Olympic Games.
Arthurson and Quayle were the two key players for the ARL in their long and ultimately unsuccessful battle for control of the sport with media magnate Rupert Murdoch's Super League.
Arthurson, who resigned as executive chairman of the ARL a year ago, told a news conference doctors had already advised him to ease his workload.
"The reality is that the workload has increased. It is inevitable that it will increase further and I need to step aside," Arthurson said.
The ARL fought for almost two years to try to thwart Murdoch before a court appeal ruled that Super League had the legal right to operate in Australia.
As a result, the existing ARL premiership will kick off this year in direct competition with Super League, dividing clubs and supporters between the two camps.

Super League was created by Murdoch's News Ltd, the Australian arm of his media empire, with the aim of ultimately forcing the ARL to fold or compromise. Super League matches will be broadcast on Murdoch's pay television interests worldwide.
